samples.summary: New `findOutermostTableId` in `text-editor.ts` is a fourth copy of the "walk `blockParentMap` up to the top-level table" loop. The same walk already exists in `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:487-495), inline in `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:146-157) and in `peer-cursor.ts:118-126`. The change's own lessons doc (`docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-lessons.md`, "Two lookups for one table") concludes that when two neighbours resolve the same thing two ways the weaker one is a latent bug — yet the fix extracts a *private* helper instead of exporting one shared walk from `table-layout.ts` next to the resolver everything else already imports. Cost stays inside the codebase (the copies behave alike today), but it re-creates exactly the divergence the fix was written to remove.

samples.summary: The cycle guard the change introduces is applied to only three of the five identical parent-chain walks. `resolveNestedTableLayout`, `findOuterCellAddress` and the new `findOutermostTableId` now carry a `seen` set, but the two structurally identical walks in `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:147-157, which runs on every render for every selection) and `peer-cursor.ts:118-126` are untouched. If the stated rationale ("a peer-written cyclic parent chain would hang the tab") holds, it holds for those loops too — they only terminate on a missing parent, which a 2-cycle never produces. Either the hardening belongs on the shared walk (see the duplication finding) or the rationale is over-stated for the ones that got it.

finding.summary: Shift+click cell-range parity is only implemented for top-level tables, leaving the nested-table case (the very case the other half of this PR fixes) still collapsing the caret
finding.evidence: The new arm is guarded by `anchorCellInfo && anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId === pos.blockId`, where `pos.blockId` is necessarily a TOP-LEVEL table block (the enclosing branch resolves `clickedBlock` from `this.doc.document.blocks.find(...)`, text-editor.ts:2023-2025). For an anchor inside a NESTED table, `anchorCellInfo.tableBlockId` is the inner table id, so the condition is false and control falls to the pre-existing `else` that moves the caret and clears the selection (2104-2108). The drag path handles exactly this case explicitly — `resolvedCellInfo.tableBlockId === anchorTableId` → "Different cell in the SAME table (e.g., inner table cell-range selection)" (2399-2417) — and also handles the outer-table fallback via `findOuterCellAddress` (2418-2431), neither of which the shift+click arm mirrors. The task plan's acceptance (docs/tasks/active/20260914-table-drag-merge-selection-todo.md:46-47, "shift+click across rows produces the same rectangle as the equivalent drag") therefore holds only for top-level tables; a user shift+clicking across cells of a nested table still gets no cell range, which is the same gesture/nesting mismatch #1049 is about.

verdict.reason: The claimed top-level-only guard does not exist. The shift+click cell arm (text-editor.ts:2082-2118) is guarded only by `anchorCellInfo` being present (2093-2095) and delegates to the shared helper `this.resolveCellGesture(anchor.blockId, anchorCellInfo, pos.blockId, cellAddr, mouseX, mouseY)` — the exact same helper the drag path calls at 2381-2383. That helper (3942-4002) resolves the endpoint through `resolveOffsetInCellAtXY` and `layout.blockParentMap`, and contains both branches the finding says shift+click fails to mirror: the nested/same-inner-table cell-range branch at 3956-3983 ("Different cell in the SAME table (e.g., inner table cell-range selection)", building the range on the inner `anchorTableId` via `expandCellRangeForMerges`) and the outer-table fallback via `findOuterCellAddress` at 3987-4001. A grep for `tableBlockId === pos.blockId` across packages/docs/src returns no hits, and `resolveCellGesture` has exactly three occurrences (shift+click call, drag call, definition). The `else` at 2114-2118 is therefore reached only when the shared resolver returns `undefined`, i.e. the same no-cell condition the drag path also yields nothing for — not for any nested-anchor case.
